Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>

Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>

title: HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Modern enterprise networks operate under persistent threats that exploit cloud-native misconfigurations, identity sprawl, and API vulnerabilities at machine speed. Existing security operations center (SOC) architectures remain largely reactive, signature-dependent, and incapable of predicting multi-stage lateral movement. This paper proposes the Cognitive Cyber Defense Digital Twin (CCDT), a unified architecture integrating federated learning (FL), graph neural network (GNN)-based attack-path forecasting, adversarially hardened detection models, and autonomous Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) with deception engineering. The CCDT constructs a continuously synchronized digital replica of organizational assets and employs reinforcement learning-based red agents to stress-test detection models. A federated intelligence mesh enables cross-organizational privacy-preserving gradient sharing. Experimental evaluations against CICIDS-2018 and LANL datasets demonstrate 52% faster attack-path detection, 41% reduction in false positive rate, and 60% reduction in mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) compared to traditional SOC baselines. Integrated Explainable AI (XAI) modules using SHAP values enable audit-ready compliance reporting. The CCDT represents a paradigm shift from reactive monitoring to predictive, autonomous, and privacy-preserving cyber defense for hybrid cloud environments.</jats:p>

title: Transforming Education through Technology: The Case of COVID 19 Digital Learning in Nagaland
abstract:
<jats:p>Through the perspective of the COVID-19 pandemic and the disruption and opportunity it engendered, this chapter follows a transformative effect of EdTech and Digital education in India particularly in Nagaland through analysis. Drawing upon national policy frameworks, conceptual literature on educational technology, and contextual evidence based on the case of Nagaland, the chapter considers the rapid migration to digital learning as an emergency strategy (in response to the ongoing institution closures) based on the stark shifts in pedagogical practice, access to education services, and preparedness. The findings show that, including the ability of national programmes such as NEP 2020, SWAYAM, DIKSHA, PM e-VIDYA, and others, to promote access to digital tools was low within periphery or hill areas (e.g., Nagaland), due to lack of infrastructural resources, digital divide, unprepared teachers and economic/social divides, and more. The pandemic exposed the deep social and infrastructure divides in connectivity, device availability, assessment and learner engagement, with implications that were especially grave in rural and tribal settings. Although it accelerated the pace of innovation and the application of blended and low-tech learning practices teachers have been experimenting with digital platforms and the post-COVID recovery process, including remedial programmes and hybrid instruction. The chapter also discusses that blended learning is the most fitting, viable and sustainable approach for reaching the technological level in the field of educational technology at Nagaland. It implies that technology-mediated education can improve equity, quality, and resilience, but only under the conditions of inclusive policy design, strong digital infrastructure, vigorous teacher capability building, and culturally appropriate digital content.

title: Automatic Detection and Counting of Surgical Instruments in Surgery Using AI-Based Computer Vision Model.
abstract: IntroductionCounting surgical instruments during surgical procedures is critical for ensuring patient safety. Our goal is to develop a machine learning-based computer vision algorithm to create a reliable, automated surgical instrument counting support system. We hypothesize that our machine learning algorithm, based on the YOLO (You Only Look Once) model, can effectively perform instrument counting in surgery videos, providing real-time feedback to the surgical team.MethodsYOLO is a real-time object detection algorithm built on a convolutional neural network (CNN). To train the model, we record 100 minutes of open surgery video in simulation, including 600 instrument transfer events. Additionally, we collected 500 images of 6 different surgical instruments and obtained another 500 images from online surgeries. All images were annotated by a human expert to mark the name and locations of instruments. 80% data was allocated for model training and 20% for validation. Trained YOLO model was tested in a new surgical video for counting surgical instruments.ResultsThe model achieved a satisfactory accuracy rate for instrument detection and counting. In a validation session, the model demonstrated a 72.7% success rate. In addition, the model classified large instruments more successfully than smaller instruments, such as small hemostats and needles, within the defined ROI.ConclusionYOLOv11-based computer vision model can accurately detect and count surgical instruments within a predefined region of interest in a simulated open surgical environment. Future research should focus on improving detection of small instruments, validating the system in real operating room environments.

title: Deep learning assessment of visualization in rotator cuff repair: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial comparing epinephrine irrigation and intravenous tranexamic acid.
abstract: This study aimed to compare intraoperative visualization between diluted epinephrine (EPN) irrigation and preoperative intravenous tranexamic acid (TXA) during the glenohumeral and subacromial phases of rotator cuff repair. Eighty-two patients with rotator cuff tears were prospectively randomized (1:1) to receive either 0.33 mg/L EPN irrigation without TXA (EPN group) or preoperative intravenous TXA (15 mg/kg) without EPN irrigation (TXA group). Visual clarity was evaluated using a pretrained deep learning model with a 3-point grading scale across three stages: intra-articular assessment, subacromial debridement, and rotator cuff repair. Irrigation pump pressure was recorded at each stage. Hypotensive bradycardic events (HBEs) and postoperative adverse events were monitored. Overall visual clarity was significantly greater in the EPN group than in the TXA group (mean difference [MD], 0.07; 95% CI, 0.03-0.10; P<0.001). Visualization was superior with EPN during subacromial debridement (MD, 0.08; 95% CI, 0.03-0.13; P=0.001) and rotator cuff repair (MD, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.004-0.06; P=0.02). The EPN group required lower pump pressures and fewer increases in pressure. No significant differences in HBEs or adverse events were observed. Diluted EPN irrigation improved intraoperative visualization compared with TXA, particularly during the subacromial phases, without increasing perioperative risk. Deep learning provided objective support for its clinical use. Level of evidence: II.

title: Trust, Traits, and Turning Points: Decoding Operator Responses to Real-World ADAS Malfunctions.
abstract: OCCUPATIONAL APPLICATIONThis study found that high emotional trust in Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) showed a non-significant tendency toward slower manual intervention during malfunctions, and that an operator's personality was related to specific information needs. For practitioners, this indicates a critical safety gap where affective comfort, feeling "too safe" reduces readiness. To mitigate these risks, organizations should prioritize hands-on, simulated malfunction training. By exposing operators to controlled scenarios such as "phantom braking" events, practitioners can help them experience system limitations firsthand, rebuilding the protective skepticism and preparedness that sustained automation use tends to erode. Because occupational driving spans a range of operational models, safety protocols should be tailored accordingly. In managed fleets, organizations have an opportunity to implement personality-aligned Human-Machine Interface (HMI) configurations that address the specific cognitive and informational needs of individual drivers. For "Bring Your Own Device" (BYOD) gig platforms, where organizations cannot modify the vehicle's native systems, broader software-based interventions are more practical, for example, in-app geofenced warnings that alert drivers as they approach known ADAS limitation zones. Together, these targeted, context-sensitive interventions help recalibrate trust and prevent overreliance, supporting rapid recovery and sustained situational awareness across the diverse occupational contexts in which ADAS is now used.

title: Mast Cell Infiltration Helps Distinguish Fibrosing Alopecia in a Pattern Distribution From Androgenetic Alopecia in Scalp Biopsy.
abstract: Mast cells are key regulators of cutaneous inflammation and are known to accumulate in response to various immunological stimuli. Although their role in several dermatological conditions has been established, their specific contribution to different forms of alopecia-particularly scarring versus nonscarring types-remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to compare the degree of mast cell infiltration across three distinct types of alopecia: androgenetic alopecia (AGA), fibrosing alopecia in a pattern distribution (FAPD), and lichen planopilaris (LPP). A total of 56 patients diagnosed with AGA, FAPD, or LPP were enrolled. Scalp biopsies were obtained from all participants, and diagnoses were confirmed through histopathological examination. Mast cell distribution and infiltration density were quantified and analyzed using SPSS and Stata software. The study was conducted with full ethical approval. The majority of participants (91%) were female, with a mean age of 44.3 years. FAPD was the most prevalent diagnosis (42.9%). LPP demonstrated the highest degree of mast cell infiltration, while AGA exhibited the lowest (ANOVA, p < 0.001). Post hoc analysis revealed significant differences between AGA and FAPD (-17.7%, p = 0.001) and between AGA and LPP (-20.1%, p = 0.001). Although mast cell infiltration was higher in patients over 40 years of age, this difference did not reach statistical significance. No significant association was identified between mast cell infiltration and patient sex. Mast cell infiltration is significantly more pronounced in scarring alopecias (LPP and FAPD) compared to non-scarring AGA, suggesting a shared immunopathological mechanism underlying follicular destruction in scarring subtypes. These findings also raise important questions regarding the potential inflammatory contribution of mast cells to AGA pathogenesis.

GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending them to domain-intensive mechanistic investigations remains challenging. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs). Although general GBs constitute the vast majority of real-world interfaces in polycrystalline materials, they remain understudied because their structural complexity and interfacial mismatch complicate experimental and modeling research. GBClaw integrates large language models (LLMs) into a modular architecture comprising an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain-specific tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory. Through dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement, the framework effectively connects systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, GBClaw characterized interfacial defect structures and identified diverse deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. Comparing boundary sliding with and without secondary GB misfit dislocations revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of defect hierarchies in sliding resistance. Furthermore, researcher-guided follow-up calculations traced an anomalously high shear resistance to metastable boundary structures. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening with deep physical understanding of complex material interfaces.
ai_summary: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design . Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs)

title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
abstract: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.
ai_summary: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion . But it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene . Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig .

title: UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control
abstract: Motivated by the human ability to integrate experience across language, perception, and action, we introduce UniWALM, a unified world-action-language model that learns video, action, and language in a single shared representation, where each modality is both a conditioning signal and a supervision target. We ask: can jointly generating language enrich this shared representation, improving manipulation and supporting memory-dependent behavior? Unlike prior approaches that attach a reasoning or vision-language model to a video-action backbone and run them as distinct stages, UniWALM unifies all three modalities inside a single mixture-of-transformers backbone whose per-modality diffusion heads co-denoise synchronously, decoding subtask and textual memory in the same pass as action with no separate planning stage; the generated language is re-consumed on the next step, closing a language-as-memory loop without an external planner or memory bank. To keep the action stream reliable under this richer objective, we further introduce Flow Matching with Correction (FMC), a training objective that teaches recovery from perturbed action trajectories at no inference-time cost. UniWALM consistently improves over same-backbone baselines (e.g., FastWAM) on compositional pick-and-place (MolmoSpaces) and across the memory-dependent subset of RMBench, where it reaches 34.5% without any pretrained language or reasoning model and exceeds Mem-0's keyframe-equipped setup (28.5%) using only a single anchor frame. On a real-world Find-the-Item task, generating textual memory lifts success from 11.1% to 61.1%, while state-of-the-art VLAs stay at or below chance (<=33.3%).
ai_summary: UniWALM is a unified world-action-language model that learns video, action, and language in a single shared representation . Each modality is both a conditioning signal and a supervision target .

title: Learning Adaptable Dexterous Skills via Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking
abstract: Dexterous multi-finger hands hold promise to unlock diverse skills like functional grasps, in-hand reorientation, and dynamic handover that the human-designed world assumes, yet existing learning recipes force a trade-off. Goal-reaching reinforcement learning generalizes to arbitrary object poses but, lacking any human prior, converges to unnatural and unreliable finger strategies; motion tracking reproduces human-like behavior from a single clip but cannot deviate from it. We present AdaDex, a goal-conditioned RL framework that turns a single hand-object trajectory of a few seconds---from mocap data or HOI reconstruction from in-the-wild RGB(D) video---into an adaptable dexterous skill. At the core of AdaDex is Hybrid Dexterous Mimicking: a shared policy is trained on two populations of massively parallel environments: motion tracking environments trained with dense motion tracking objective, which instill the human prior from human motion; and generalization environments with noised initial states and goals and a sparse object-success reward, which force the skill to work far off the reference. From seconds of human motion per skill, the resulting policies can learn diverse adaptable dexterous skills, such as functional grasping, object reposing, in-hand reorientation with finger gaiting, and dynamic behaviors like throw-and-catch. Our method outperforms baselines in terms of generalization and functionality, and we demonstrate transfer across simulators and to the real world. Project page: https://yuxuank.com/AdaDex/.
